windows.why: Unchanged. The two stages now in the rotation burn $32/h (resolver, measured over the 11h Sep 27-28 burst) and ~$35/h (acuity, 79 windows/h x $0.442), so 5h of flat-out work is ~$175. This cannot throttle the run; it exists only to stop a loop.

Raised from $3,000 on 2026-10-02 for the unsupervised multi-day run, because at $3,000 it WOULD have bound mid-run and stopped with nobody there to raise it. The plan is 688 divination claims (229 calls x $1.793 = $411) plus 5,548 acuity windows; acuity's per-call cost is unmeasured, so the ceiling is sized on the measured six-attribute figure of $0.442/call = $2,452, an upper bound (the acuity system prompt is 3,740 tokens against 7,469, and the dry run estimates $0.111/call). Worst case $2,863, plus up to $642 of this week's spend still inside the rolling window = $3,505. $4,500 leaves headroom without being unbounded.

note: NO RESERVE, set 2026-09-19; 168h ceiling raised 2026-10-02. These are a runaway guard, not a throttle -- the real limit is the subscription's rolling session cap, which is readable from nowhere and is handled by overnight_run's QuotaExhausted backoff. Dollar figures are list-price accounting of subscription usage, not billed amounts. If a daytime reserve is wanted again, the number that matters is the 5h cap.
